claims.text: The as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu coating is polycrystalline and fine-grained.
At elevated temperatures, the wear resistance of FeNiCrCoCu thin-film coatings is governed by temperature-activated dynamic recrystallization at grain boundaries.
Dynamic recrystallization at grain boundaries produces a dense, hardened tribolayer.
The dynamically formed tribolayer has low friction.
Elevated temperature promotes grain-boundary sliding and reorganization in the coating.
Grain-boundary sliding and reorganization cause in-situ formation of a protective tribolayer.
The protective tribolayer increases local hardness.
Increased local hardness and reduced friction enhance the coating's wear resistance.
At approximately 300–400 °C, the coating will have greater hardness than under otherwise identical room-temperature conditions.
At approximately 300–400 °C, the coating will have a lower friction coefficient than under otherwise identical room-temperature conditions.
At approximately 300–400 °C, tribolayer formation, increased hardness, and lower friction will correlate with improved wear resistance relative to room temperature.
Above an optimum temperature, grain coarsening undermines the protective effect of the tribolayer.
At temperatures above approximately 500 °C, grain growth will diminish the protective mechanism and reduce wear performance.
The proposed mechanism applies to FeNiCrCoCu thin films under wear-mimicking nanoindentation loads in the range of 300–600 °C.
